title: PATRICIA binary trie
summary: In 1968, Morrison and Gwehenberger described a binary trie that records only the distinguishing bit at each branch, compressing paths while supporting keyed retrieval.

parents.reason: PATRICIA is a radix-2 trie variant: it preserves trie branching by key prefixes while skipping nondiscriminating bits.

title: Bachman data-structure diagrams
summary: Charles Bachman's 1969 diagrams represented logical data structures and record relationships separately from their physical storage arrangement.

title: Suffix tree indexing
summary: Weiner's 1973 suffix-tree concept indexed every text suffix through trie-based prefix identifiers, enabling fast substring operations; later compressed forms reduced its space and construction cost.

parents.reason: Weiner's original construction stored suffix-position identifiers in a trie and extended trie structures to index all suffixes of a text.

title: Aho–Corasick multi-pattern matching
summary: Aho and Corasick's 1975 algorithm matched many dictionary strings in one text pass by adding failure-transition links to a trie-derived finite-state machine.

parents.reason: The algorithm first builds trie paths for the dictionary strings, then augments their shared-prefix structure with fallback links.
Its added transitions turn the dictionary trie into a finite-state machine that continues matching without backtracking.

title: Crow's-foot relationship notation
summary: Gordon Everest's 1976 notation used crow-foot line ends to show relationship cardinalities in data-structure diagrams.

parents.reason: The ER-model history says crow's-foot relationship lines in some diagrams owed more to earlier Bachman diagrams than to Chen's original diagrams.

title: Suffix automaton
summary: The 1983 suffix automaton compactly represented all suffixes of a string as a minimal partial deterministic finite automaton, supporting substring-index operations.

parents.reason: The structure is defined as a minimal partial deterministic finite automaton recognizing the suffixes of its input string.

title: Compacted suffix automaton
summary: In 1987, Blumer and colleagues compressed redundant suffix-automaton states to create the compacted suffix automaton, also called a CDAWG.

parents.reason: The compacted structure is made by removing nonfinal automaton states with a single outgoing arc and retaining the language index.
The authors explicitly applied the state-compression technique used in suffix trees to the suffix automaton to form the compacted structure.

title: Suffix array indexing
summary: Manber and Myers introduced suffix arrays in 1990 as a space-efficient sorted-index alternative to suffix trees for string-search operations.

parents.reason: Suffix arrays were explicitly introduced as a lower-space alternative to suffix trees while supporting related string-indexing operations.

title: Longest-common-prefix array
summary: Manber and Myers's 1993 publication described using common-prefix lengths of adjacent sorted suffixes to speed string searches.

parents.reason: Each LCP entry records the shared-prefix length of adjacent suffixes in the suffix array, augmenting that sorted index for faster searches.

title: System R cost-based query optimization
summary: The 1979 System R access-path work pioneered dynamic-programming join-order selection, comparing scan and index alternatives to choose efficient query plans.

parents.reason: IBM's System R database project developed the join-order optimization procedure used as the pattern for most later relational query optimizers.
The optimizer evaluates reusable best subplans for relation subsets to search join orders without enumerating every complete plan independently.

title: IDEF1 information-modeling method
summary: Published by the ICAM program in 1981, IDEF1 represented the structure and semantics of information in an environment and supplied the initial method later extended as IDEF1X.

parents.reason: The IDEF1 history identifies Chen's entity–relationship model as one of the theoretical roots for its 1981 information-modeling approach.
The IDEF1 history identifies Codd's relational-model theory as a separate theoretical root for the 1981 method.

title: IDEF1X data-modeling standard
summary: NIST's 1993 FIPS 184 publication standardized IDEF1X, an integrated, database-neutral information model that could be transformed into user views and physical database designs.

parents.reason: IDEF1X was the Air Force method relabeled after accepted extensions to the original IDEF1 information-modeling technique; the 1993 FIPS publication standardized that evolved method.

title: Codd's named OLAP formulation
summary: Codd's 1993 twelve-rule white paper gave the name and proposed criteria for OLAP after a consulting assignment for Arbor Software, whose Essbase product had appeared in 1992.

parents.reason: The paper that coined OLAP explicitly referred to Essbase features and arose from Codd's consulting assignment for its developer Arbor Software.

title: Essbase multidimensional database
summary: Arbor Software's Essbase, first released in 1992, stored multidimensional business data for analytic applications beyond the limits of spreadsheet-only models.

title: Linear direct construction of CDAWGs
summary: Crochemore and Vérin's 1997 algorithm constructed a compacted directed acyclic word graph directly in linear time.

parents.reason: The algorithm directly constructs the compacted suffix automaton (CDAWG), rather than first building and then compressing a regular suffix automaton.

title: Trie-input CDAWG construction
summary: In 2001, Inenaga and colleagues described constructing a CDAWG for a set of words supplied as a trie, avoiding an explicit list of the represented strings.

parents.reason: The 2001 method takes a trie as the input representation of the word set and traverses its prefix structure to build the resulting automaton.
parents.directContribution: This is an independent direct input: the 2001 construction consumes and traverses the trie representing the word set, rather than receiving that input through the suffix-tree route to the same automaton.

parents.reason: The constructed result is the compacted suffix automaton generalization for the set of words represented by the input trie.

title: Powersort adaptive mergesort
summary: Munro and Wild's 2018 Powersort replaced Timsort's run-merging heuristic with a nearly optimal policy that adapts stably to existing order in the input.

parents.reason: Powersort builds on Timsort and replaces its suboptimal heuristic for choosing which ordered runs to merge, while reusing its merge implementation.
